title: Days After Part A Coverage Ends in a Notice-Billed Month: Advance Beneficiary Notice Choices and Pending Expedited Reviews
content:
Under Medical Assistance Nursing Facility Coverage, an actual-billed month can contain days after the resident's Medicare Part A Skilled Nursing Facility Coverage stopped covering the stay. Those days are taken out of the month — they carry no cost — when the resident pays for them or Medicare is still deciding.

**Formal clause.** Days of an actual-billed month after Part A coverage ended that the resident pays, or that Medicare is still deciding: where the resident's coverage in status coverage ended or closed with the latest last covered date ended inside the month and the latest Skilled Nursing Facility Advance Beneficiary Notice, by delivery date, recorded on it has the resident's choice of option 1 or option 2 (the care goes on and the resident pays for it), the days of the month from the first non-covered date it names; where the resident's coverage in status under appeal has its last covered date before the month's end, the days of the month after that last covered date, which are not billed while the timely expedited review is pending; otherwise none (option 3, no notice, or no coverage ending), since those days are Medicaid days. Either span stops at the day before a hospice election inside the month. Where two notices share the latest delivery date, the one posted first is read.

**Basis Q&A.**

*The coverage ended inside the month and the latest notice records option 1.* The days from the first non-covered date the notice names through the month's end are taken out — or through the day before the hospice election date, where an election falls inside the month.

*The latest notice records option 2.* The same as option 1: the care goes on and the resident pays for it, so those days are taken out.

*The latest notice records option 3, or no notice is recorded, or the coverage did not end inside the month.* No day is taken out on this ground; those days are Medicaid days.

*A coverage is under appeal and its last covered date is before the month's end.* The days after the last covered date are taken out, up to the month's end or the day before a hospice election inside the month.

**Hypothetical counting.** In a 30-day month, a coverage that ended inside the month carries a latest notice recording option 2 and naming day 12 as the first non-covered date: days 12 to 30, 19 days, are taken out. With a hospice election on day 21 instead, days 12 to 20, 9 days, are taken out.
